lr_all <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pair_index)), function(i) {
  x <- computeLRContributions(inp$Lmatrix, inp$Rmatrix, inp$Cmatrix, inp$LRmatrix,
                              celltypes, sender = pair_index$Sender[i],
                              receiver = pair_index$Receiver[i], bundle = FALSE,
                              patient_names = patients)
  if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)
  as.data.table(x)[, .(Patient, Sender, Receiver, Ligand, Receptor, Contribution, PctOfTotal)]
}))
# sanity check: contributions add up to the kernel score of each cell-type pair

meta <- meta[match(patients, rna_id), .(Patient = rna_id, Response, Therapy)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(meta$Patient))

# ---- 1. Kernel: direct communication ---------------------------------------
run_kernel <- function(norm, remove_direction) {
  suppressWarnings(compute_racing_kernel(input_data = inp, norm = norm,
                                         remove_direction = remove_direction))
}
dir_raw  <- run_kernel(norm = FALSE, remove_direction = FALSE)  # sender -> receiver
dir_norm <- run_kernel(norm = TRUE,  remove_direction = FALSE)  # enrichment vs uniform LR baseline
und_raw  <- run_kernel(norm = FALSE, remove_direction = TRUE)   # both directions merged
stopifnot(identical(rownames(dir_raw$features), patients))

write.csv(dir_raw$features,  file.path(k_dir, "direct_communication_directed_raw.csv"))
write.csv(dir_norm$features, file.path(k_dir, "direct_communication_directed_normalized.csv"))
write.csv(und_raw$features,  file.path(k_dir, "direct_communication_undirected_raw.csv"))
saveRDS(list(directed_raw = dir_raw, directed_norm = dir_norm, undirected_raw = und_raw),
        file.path(k_dir, "racing_kernel_results.rds"))

# ---- 2. Cohort-level ranking of cell-type pairs ----------------------------
# feature name -> (sender, receiver); cell-type names contain no "_"
pair_index <- CJ(Sender = celltypes, Receiver = celltypes, sorted = FALSE)
pair_index[, Feature := paste0("Dir_", Sender, "_", Receiver)]

summarise_features <- function(feat, top_k = 5) {
  feat <- as.matrix(feat)
  share <- feat / rowSums(feat)  # fraction of each patient's total direct communication
  rk <- t(apply(-share, 1, rank, ties.method = "min"))
  data.table(
    Feature            = colnames(feat),
    Mean               = colMeans(feat),
    Median             = apply(feat, 2, median),
    Q1                 = apply(feat, 2, quantile, 0.25),
    Q3                 = apply(feat, 2, quantile, 0.75),
    MedianPctOfTotal   = 100 * apply(share, 2, median),
    PctPatientsDetected = 100 * colMeans(feat > 0),
    PctPatientsAbove1pct = 100 * colMeans(share >= 0.01),
    MedianRankInPatient = apply(rk, 2, median),
    PctPatientsTop5    = 100 * colMeans(rk <= top_k)
  )
}

dir_sum <- summarise_features(dir_raw$features)
dir_sum <- merge(pair_index, dir_sum, by = "Feature")
norm_med <- apply(as.matrix(dir_norm$features), 2, median)
dir_sum[, MedianEnrichment := norm_med[Feature]]
dir_sum[, Interaction := paste0(pretty_ct[Sender], " -> ", pretty_ct[Receiver])]
setorder(dir_sum, -Median)
dir_sum[, CohortRank := .I]
setcolorder(dir_sum, c("CohortRank", "Interaction", "Sender", "Receiver", "Feature"))
fwrite(dir_sum, file.path(s_dir, "celltype_pairs_directed_ranking.csv"))

und_sum <- summarise_features(und_raw$features)
und_pairs <- pair_index[Feature %in% und_sum$Feature]
und_sum <- merge(und_pairs, und_sum, by = "Feature")
und_sum[, Interaction := paste0(pretty_ct[Sender], " <-> ", pretty_ct[Receiver])]
setorder(und_sum, -Median)
und_sum[, CohortRank := .I]
setcolorder(und_sum, c("CohortRank", "Interaction", "Sender", "Receiver", "Feature"))
fwrite(und_sum, file.path(s_dir, "celltype_pairs_undirected_ranking.csv"))

# per-sender / per-receiver totals (outgoing and incoming communication)
role <- rbind(
  dir_sum[, .(Role = "Sender (outgoing)", MedianOfSum = NA_real_), by = .(CellType = Sender)],
  dir_sum[, .(Role = "Receiver (incoming)", MedianOfSum = NA_real_), by = .(CellType = Receiver)]
)
feat_mat <- as.matrix(dir_raw$features)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(role))) {
  cols <- if (role$Role[i] == "Sender (outgoing)") dir_sum[Sender == role$CellType[i], Feature]
          else dir_sum[Receiver == role$CellType[i], Feature]
  role$MedianOfSum[i] <- median(rowSums(feat_mat[, cols, drop = FALSE]))
}
role[, CellTypeLabel := pretty_ct[CellType]]
role[, MedianAbundance := apply(inp$Cmatrix, 2, median)[CellType]]
fwrite(role[order(Role, -MedianOfSum)], file.path(s_dir, "celltype_sender_receiver_totals.csv"))

# per-patient top interactions
pt_top <- rbindlist(lapply(patients, function(p) {
  v <- feat_mat[p, ]; o <- order(-v)[1:5]
  data.table(Patient = p, Rank = 1:5, Feature = names(v)[o], Score = v[o],
             PctOfTotal = 100 * v[o] / sum(v))
}))
pt_top <- merge(pt_top, dir_sum[, .(Feature, Interaction)], by = "Feature")
pt_top <- merge(pt_top, meta, by = "Patient")
setorder(pt_top, Patient, Rank)
fwrite(pt_top[, .(Patient, Response, Therapy, Rank, Interaction, Score, PctOfTotal)],
       file.path(s_dir, "per_patient_top5_interactions.csv"))
top1 <- pt_top[Rank == 1, .N, by = Interaction][order(-N)]
top1[, PctPatients := 100 * N / length(patients)]
fwrite(top1, file.path(s_dir, "most_frequent_top1_interaction.csv"))

# ---- 3. Ligand-receptor pairs behind each cell-type pair --------------------
lr_all <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pair_index)), function(i) {
  x <- computeLRContributions(inp$Lmatrix, inp$Rmatrix, inp$Cmatrix, inp$LRmatrix,
                              celltypes, sender = pair_index$Sender[i],
                              receiver = pair_index$Receiver[i], bundle = FALSE,
                              patient_names = patients)
  if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)
  as.data.table(x)[, .(Patient, Sender, Receiver, Ligand, Receptor, Contribution, PctOfTotal)]
}))
# sanity check: contributions add up to the kernel score of each cell-type pair
chk <- lr_all[, .(S = sum(Contribution)), by = .(Patient, Sender, Receiver)]
chk[, K := feat_mat[cbind(Patient, paste0("Dir_", Sender, "_", Receiver))]]
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$S - chk$K)) < 1e-10)
fwrite(lr_all, file.path(lr_dir, "lr_contributions_all_pairs_all_patients.csv.gz"))

n_pt <- length(patients)
lr_all[, LR := paste0(Ligand, "-", Receptor)]

# (a) LR pairs ranked within each sender->receiver pair (missing = 0 contribution)
lr_by_pair <- lr_all[, .(MeanContribution = sum(Contribution) / n_pt,
                         MeanPctOfPair = sum(PctOfTotal) / n_pt,
                         PctPatientsPresent = 100 * .N / n_pt),
                     by = .(Sender, Receiver, Ligand, Receptor, LR)]
lr_by_pair[, Interaction := paste0(pretty_ct[Sender], " -> ", pretty_ct[Receiver])]
setorder(lr_by_pair, Sender, Receiver, -MeanContribution)
lr_by_pair[, RankInPair := seq_len(.N), by = .(Sender, Receiver)]
fwrite(lr_by_pair, file.path(lr_dir, "lr_pairs_per_celltype_pair.csv"))

top_pairs <- dir_sum[1:10, .(Sender, Receiver, CohortRank)]
lr_top_pairs <- merge(lr_by_pair[RankInPair <= 10], top_pairs, by = c("Sender", "Receiver"))
setorder(lr_top_pairs, CohortRank, RankInPair)
fwrite(lr_top_pairs, file.path(lr_dir, "top10_LR_pairs_for_top10_celltype_pairs.csv"))

# (b) LR pairs ranked over all communication (summed over cell-type pairs)
pt_total <- rowSums(feat_mat)
lr_pt <- lr_all[, .(Contribution = sum(Contribution)), by = .(Patient, Ligand, Receptor, LR)]
lr_pt[, PctOfPatientTotal := 100 * Contribution / pt_total[Patient]]
lr_pt[, RankInPatient := frank(-Contribution, ties.method = "min"), by = Patient]
lr_global <- lr_pt[, .(MeanPctOfTotal = sum(PctOfPatientTotal) / n_pt,
                       MedianPctOfTotal = median(c(PctOfPatientTotal, rep(0, n_pt - .N))),
                       PctPatientsTop20 = 100 * sum(RankInPatient <= 20) / n_pt,
                       PctPatientsPresent = 100 * .N / n_pt),
                   by = .(Ligand, Receptor, LR)]
main_pair <- lr_all[, .(C = sum(Contribution)), by = .(LR, Sender, Receiver)][
  order(-C), .(MainCellPair = paste0(pretty_ct[Sender[1]], " -> ", pretty_ct[Receiver[1]]),
               MainCellPairPct = 100 * C[1] / sum(C)), by = LR]
lr_global <- merge(lr_global, main_pair, by = "LR")
setorder(lr_global, -MeanPctOfTotal)
lr_global[, CohortRank := .I]
setcolorder(lr_global, "CohortRank")
fwrite(lr_global, file.path(lr_dir, "lr_pairs_global_ranking.csv"))

# ---- 4. Figures -------------------------------------------------------------
save_plot <- function(p, name, w, h) {
  ggsave(file.path(f_dir, paste0(name, ".pdf")), p, width = w, height = h)
  ggsave(file.path(f_dir, paste0(name, ".png")), p, width = w, height = h, dpi = 200)
}
ct_order <- names(pretty_ct)[names(pretty_ct) %in% celltypes]
hm <- copy(dir_sum)[, `:=`(SenderL = factor(pretty_ct[Sender], pretty_ct[ct_order]),
                           ReceiverL = factor(pretty_ct[Receiver], pretty_ct[ct_order]))]

p1 <- ggplot(hm, aes(ReceiverL, SenderL, fill = MedianPctOfTotal)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", MedianPctOfTotal)), size = 2.8) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "firebrick", name = "% of total\n(median)") +
  labs(x = "Receiver", y = "Sender",
       title = "RaCInG direct communication - Gide cohort (n = 73)",
       subtitle = "Median % of each patient's total direct communication") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
save_plot(p1, "heatmap_directed_communication_median", 7.5, 6)

p2 <- ggplot(hm, aes(ReceiverL, SenderL, fill = log2(MedianEnrichment))) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", MedianEnrichment)), size = 2.6) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "steelblue", mid = "white", high = "firebrick",
                       name = "log2 median\nenrichment") +
  labs(x = "Receiver", y = "Sender",
       title = "Communication enrichment vs. uniform ligand-receptor baseline",
       subtitle = "Median ratio across patients (1 = expected from abundance/topology)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
save_plot(p2, "heatmap_directed_enrichment_median", 7.5, 6)

top20 <- dir_sum[1:20]
long20 <- melt(as.data.table(feat_mat[, top20$Feature], keep.rownames = "Patient"),
               id.vars = "Patient", variable.name = "Feature", value.name = "Score")
long20 <- merge(long20, top20[, .(Feature, Interaction)], by = "Feature")
long20[, Interaction := factor(Interaction, rev(top20$Interaction))]
p3 <- ggplot(long20, aes(Score * 100, Interaction)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6, fill = "grey90") +
  labs(x = "% of total direct communication", y = NULL,
       title = "Top 20 directed cell-cell interactions (ranked by cohort median)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)
save_plot(p3, "boxplot_top20_directed_interactions", 7.5, 6)

und20 <- und_sum[1:20]
p3b <- ggplot(und20, aes(MedianPctOfTotal, factor(Interaction, rev(Interaction)))) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey40") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = 100 * Q1 / median(rowSums(und_raw$features)),
                     xmax = 100 * Q3 / median(rowSums(und_raw$features))), height = 0.3) +
  labs(x = "% of total communication (median, IQR approx.)", y = NULL,
       title = "Top 20 cell-type pairs, both directions merged") + theme_bw(base_size = 10)
save_plot(p3b, "barplot_top20_undirected_interactions", 7.5, 6)

# patient x interaction heatmap (top 30 directed interactions, z-scored)
top30 <- dir_sum[1:30]
mat <- t(feat_mat[, top30$Feature])
rownames(mat) <- top30$Interaction
ann <- data.frame(Response = meta$Response, Therapy = meta$Therapy, row.names = meta$Patient)
pheatmap(mat, scale = "row", annotation_col = ann, show_colnames = FALSE,
         clustering_method = "ward.D2", fontsize_row = 8,
         color = colorRampPalette(c("steelblue", "white", "firebrick"))(100),
         breaks = seq(-3, 3, length.out = 101),
         main = "Top 30 directed interactions across patients (row z-score)",
         filename = file.path(f_dir, "heatmap_patients_top30_interactions.pdf"), width = 11, height = 7)
pheatmap(mat, scale = "row", annotation_col = ann, show_colnames = FALSE,
         clustering_method = "ward.D2", fontsize_row = 8,
         color = colorRampPalette(c("steelblue", "white", "firebrick"))(100),
         breaks = seq(-3, 3, length.out = 101),
         main = "Top 30 directed interactions across patients (row z-score)",
         filename = file.path(f_dir, "heatmap_patients_top30_interactions.png"), width = 11, height = 7)

g25 <- lr_global[1:25]
p4 <- ggplot(g25, aes(MeanPctOfTotal, factor(LR, rev(LR)), fill = PctPatientsTop20)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey80", high = "darkgreen", name = "% patients\nwith LR in\ntheir top 20") +
  labs(x = "Mean % of total direct communication", y = NULL,
       title = "Top 25 ligand-receptor pairs (all cell-type pairs combined)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)
save_plot(p4, "barplot_top25_LR_pairs_global", 7.5, 6.5)

dp <- lr_top_pairs[RankInPair <= 5]
dp[, Interaction := factor(Interaction, unique(Interaction[order(CohortRank)]))]
p5 <- ggplot(dp, aes(Interaction, factor(LR, rev(unique(LR[order(CohortRank, RankInPair)]))))) +
  geom_point(aes(size = MeanPctOfPair, colour = PctPatientsPresent)) +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "orange", high = "darkred", name = "% patients\nwith pair") +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Mean % of\ncell-pair\ncommunication") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Top 5 ligand-receptor pairs of the 10 most common cell-cell interactions") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
save_plot(p5, "dotplot_top_LR_per_top10_celltype_pairs", 9, 9)

# ---- 5. Console summary -----------------------------------------------------
cat("\nTop 15 directed interactions:\n")
print(dir_sum[1:15, .(CohortRank, Interaction, MedianPctOfTotal = round(MedianPctOfTotal, 2),
                      PctPatientsTop5 = round(PctPatientsTop5), MedianEnrichment = round(MedianEnrichment, 2))])
cat("\nTop 10 undirected interactions:\n")
print(und_sum[1:10, .(CohortRank, Interaction, MedianPctOfTotal = round(MedianPctOfTotal, 2),
                      PctPatientsTop5 = round(PctPatientsTop5))])
cat("\nMost frequent #1 interaction per patient:\n"); print(top1[1:8])
cat("\nSender/receiver totals:\n"); print(role[order(Role, -MedianOfSum)])
cat("\nTop 20 LR pairs overall:\n")
print(lr_global[1:20, .(CohortRank, LR, MeanPctOfTotal = round(MeanPctOfTotal, 2),
                        PctPatientsTop20 = round(PctPatientsTop20), MainCellPair,
                        MainCellPairPct = round(MainCellPairPct))])
cat("\nTop 5 LR pairs of the top 10 directed interactions:\n")
print(lr_top_pairs[RankInPair <= 5, .(CohortRank, Interaction, LR,
                                      MeanPctOfPair = round(MeanPctOfPair, 2),
                                      PctPatientsPresent = round(PctPatientsPresent))])
cat("\nTop 10 directed interactions by enrichment (pairs with median share >= 0.5%):\n")
print(dir_sum[MedianPctOfTotal >= 0.5][order(-MedianEnrichment)][1:10,
      .(Interaction, MedianEnrichment = round(MedianEnrichment, 2), MedianPctOfTotal = round(MedianPctOfTotal, 2))])

# RaCInG cell-cell communication — Gide cohort (73 pre-treatment melanoma samples)

Scripts: `scripts/01_prepare_input.R`, `scripts/02_racing_kernel_analysis.R` (run from the project root).

## Method
- Input `data/Gide_log2TPM.txt` (log2(TPM+1)) converted back to linear TPM (`2^x - 1`), `already_normalized = TRUE`.
- Cell fractions: quanTIseq (via multideconv). The quanTIseq "other" (non-immune) fraction is kept as
  `Cancer` (= tumor + stroma, ~63% median). It is passed to RaCInG as `deconv` because multideconv's subgroup
  analysis silently drops `uncharacterized.cell` (nomenclature mismatch) and renormalizes immune cells to 100%.
- Ligand-receptor prior: liana curated OmniPath (RaCInG default, cached); expression threshold 10 TPM.
- RaCInG kernel method (direct communication, analytic): directed raw scores, directed normalized
  (enrichment vs. uniform LR baseline), undirected raw. Raw scores = abundance-weighted fraction of
  a patient's communication edges going sender -> receiver (sum ≈ 1 per patient).
- `computeLRContributions()` decomposes each sender->receiver score exactly into ligand-receptor terms.

## Files
- `racing_input/` RaCInG L/R/C/LR matrices, CC table, quanTIseq fractions, input RDS.
- `kernel/` patient x interaction feature matrices (CSV) and full kernel results (RDS).
- `summary/` cohort ranking of directed / undirected cell-type pairs, sender/receiver totals,
  per-patient top 5 interactions, frequency of each patient's #1 interaction.
- `lr_contributions/` global LR-pair ranking, LR pairs per cell-type pair, top LR pairs of the
  top 10 interactions, and the full per-patient decomposition (`.csv.gz`).
- `figures/` heatmaps (median communication, enrichment, patient clustering), box/bar/dot plots.
- `logs/` run logs.

## Caveats
- Cell-type-level results are largely driven by quanTIseq abundances (Cancer/non-immune dominates).
- LR assignments to low-abundance immune types rely on NNLS-estimated cell profiles and contain
  implausible attributions (e.g. ANGPTL3 from B cells, PDGFD/LAMA2 from NK); interpret LR pairs for
  minor cell types with caution. CD4 Tconv and DC are absent in most samples (median fraction 0).

content.text:
I ran RaCInG on all 73 pre-treatment Gide samples. The main pattern: tumor (non-immune) cells talking to themselves and with monocytes, neutrophils, NK cells and B cells. Most of that pattern comes from how many of each cell type are present. Everything is in `results/`, with a `results/README.md` describing the files.

## How I ran it
- **Input:** I converted the log2(TPM+1) data back to linear TPM, as RaCInG requires.
- **Cell fractions:** I used quanTIseq only. RaCInG's default combines several methods and gives 100+ cell-type features that are hard to interpret; quanTIseq gives 11.
- **Method:** the kernel method, which computes direct communication exactly with no random simulation. Scores are the share of each patient's communication going from a sender to a receiver cell type, weighted by how abundant each is.
- **Ligand–receptor breakdown:** I split every cell-type pair's score into its ligand–receptor pairs. The parts sum back to the totals exactly; the script checks this.

**A problem I had to work around:** with RaCInG's default settings, the tumor/non-immune compartment (about 63% of cells) was silently dropped. A naming mismatch in multideconv, the deconvolution package RaCInG uses, caused this. The immune fractions were then rescaled to fill 100%, which inflated them (e.g. 76% neutrophils in one sample). I computed the fractions myself and passed them in so that compartment is kept (labelled "Cancer/non-immune"). I also had to prefix sample IDs, because names starting with a digit broke sample matching; the outputs use the original IDs.

| # | Interaction | Median % | % of patients where it's in their top 5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cancer → Cancer | 9.1 | 89 |
| 2 | Monocytes → Cancer | 5.5 | 59 |
| 3 | Cancer → Monocytes | 4.7 | 52 |
| 4 | Cancer → Neutrophils | 2.8 | 44 |
| 5 | Monocytes → Monocytes | 2.7 | 47 |
| 6 | Neutrophils → Cancer | 2.7 | 47 |
| 7–9 | NK → Cancer, B → Cancer, Cancer → NK | 1.7–2.4 | — |

- **T cells and dendritic cells** contribute almost nothing. CD8 T cells and Tregs are under 0.5% each; CD4 helper T cells and dendritic cells have a median abundance of zero.

Communication is spread across about 1,700 pairs, so no single pair accounts for more than about 0.3% of the total. The pairs that most often rank in a patient's top 20 are:

- `lr_contributions/lr_pairs_global_ranking.csv`
- `figures/heatmap_directed_communication_median.png`
- `figures/heatmap_patients_top30_interactions.png`

content.text:
Answers based on what I did. I ran nothing further.

**1. Input data transformation**
- I converted `Gide_log2TPM.txt` from log2(TPM+1) to linear TPM (`2^x - 1`, negatives set to 0) before any step.
- **Deconvolution:** quanTIseq via multideconv needs non-log input.
- **`prepare_input_files(already_normalized = TRUE)`:** RaCInG's 10 TPM expression threshold and its NNLS cell-profile estimation assume linear TPM.
- **Ligand–receptor strengths:** RaCInG then re-logs internally (`log2(TPM+1)`), so these use log2 values, as the package intends.
- I also prefixed sample IDs with `Gide_` (see 4) and removed the prefix again in the outputs.

**2. Methods**
- **Ran:**
  - `multideconv::compute.deconvolution` (quanTIseq only).
  - `prepare_input_files`, using my own fraction matrix, RaCInG's NNLS cell expression profiles and the default cached liana/OmniPath network.
  - `compute_racing_kernel` three times: directed raw, directed normalized, undirected raw.
  - `computeLRContributions` for all 121 sender→receiver pairs.
  - My own summary tables and ggplot/pheatmap figures.
- **Skipped:**
  - Monte Carlo (`compute_racing_montecarlo`, GSCC): the kernel method gives direct communication exactly, which was the question.
  - multideconv's subgroup analysis: it dropped the tumor compartment (see 4).
  - Other deconvolution methods (CIBERSORTx needs credentials; EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq, DWLS): to keep about 11 interpretable cell types.
  - Activity-based ligand–receptor strengths (`LR_activity`): slow and optional.
  - Statistical tests by response or therapy: not requested.
  - The Riaz data: not requested.

**3. Non-default parameters**
- **`already_normalized = TRUE`:** the data was already TPM.
- **`deconv` = my own quanTIseq matrix:** this keeps the non-immune fraction, which I renamed `Cancer`. (My first run used `deconv_method = "Quantiseq"`.)
- **`norm = TRUE`** for one run: to get enrichment over a uniform ligand–receptor baseline.
- **`remove_direction = FALSE`** for the directed runs: to keep sender and receiver separate.
- **`bundle = FALSE`** in `computeLRContributions`: one direction per pair.
- **`file_name = "Gide"`** and custom output folders.
- Unchanged: `expr_threshold = 10`, `fun_LR = min`, `zero_threshold = 1`.

**4. Problems and handling**
- **"Patient names do not match" error:** multideconv applies `make.names`, turning `10_PD1_PRE` into `X10_PD1_PRE`. I fixed it by prefixing sample IDs with `Gide_`.
- **Stray files in the project root:** multideconv wrote `Results/Deconvolution_Gide.csv` and OmnipathR wrote `omnipathr-log/`. I deleted the first (the script now does this) and moved the logs to `results/logs/`.
- **Tumor compartment silently dropped:** after the default subgroup step, only 10 immune types remained. Row sums were 0.14–1 before RaCInG rescaled them to 1, which inflated immune fractions. The cause is that `uncharacterized.cell` doesn't match the nomenclature entry `uncharacterized_cell`. I fixed it by passing my own fractions.
- **A glob `rm` was blocked by permissions:** I deleted the specific files by absolute path instead.
- **Fixes to my own script:**
  - Changed ranking from raw median to median share; only ranks 8 and 9 swapped.
  - Replaced approximate error bars with true IQR of the shares.
  - Removed a deprecated ggplot function.
  - Removed NA rows from a printed table.
  - Fixed clipped plot labels.
- **Metadata warning:** `fread` warns because `colData_all.txt` has a header/column-count mismatch (an extra index column). Columns are matched by name, so I left it.
- **One diagnostic check failed:** the `Lmatrix` has no row names, so my check of whether Monocytes→Neutrophils is structurally impossible errored. I didn't fix it. Instead I confirmed that both cell types are present together in only 34 of 73 samples, which explains the median of 0.

**5. Checks**
- The ligand–receptor contributions sum to the kernel scores (maximum difference < 1e-10).
- quanTIseq fractions sum to 1 in every sample.
- Sample IDs are unique, and their order matches the kernel output rows.
- Metadata matched all 73 samples, and every cell type has a display label.
- I looked at the cell fractions, the log warnings and three of the figures.
- **Not checked:** agreement with Monte Carlo, sensitivity to the expression threshold or deconvolution method, and comparison against published results.

**6. Limits and caution**
- **Rankings mostly reflect quanTIseq abundances.** "Cancer" means all non-immune cells, including stroma, which is why COL3A1 and POSTN appear as "tumor" ligands.
- **Ligand–receptor assignment to rare immune cells is unreliable.** It depends on NNLS-estimated profiles and includes implausible cases (ANGPTL3 from B cells, PDGFD/LAMA2 from NK cells).
- **Per-patient totals are 0.76–1.0, not exactly 1.** I didn't investigate why, so the README's "≈ 1" is loose.
- **Ligand–receptor strength is bulk expression,** the minimum of ligand and receptor log-TPM. It is the same for every cell-type pair within a patient.
- **CD4 helper T cells and dendritic cells are absent in most samples,** and CD8 T cells and Tregs are very low.
- **I treated PD1 and ipi+PD1 samples as independent.** I didn't check for repeated patients.
- **Ligand–receptor results are very spread out** (no pair above about 0.3%), so their order is fragile.
- **No response-related statistics** and only one deconvolution method.

Do not compute anything new, do not rerun any method and do not change any existing result: only convert what already exists. Put the files in results/standard/. - ligands.csv: the ligands assigned to each cell type (the cell type x ligand matrix of the prepared input, "Lmatrix"), one row per assignment, with columns cell_type and ligand (not one row per patient).
- receptors.csv: the receptors assigned to each cell type ("Rmatrix"), one row per assignment, with columns cell_type and receptor (not one row per patient).
- direct_interactions.csv: the direct-interaction features of the kernel method, not normalised and without direction: one column per unordered pair of cell types, named "<cell type A> - <cell type B>" with the cell-type names exactly as in ligands.csv. This is what RaCInG returns when the direction is removed; if you only have the features with direction, a column "A - B" is A->B plus B->A, and a column "A - A" is twice A->A.

content.text: The files contain everything needed. I'll write a conversion-only script. It includes read-only checks on cell-type names, patient names and the direction-merging convention.

input.content:
# Export existing RaCInG results to a standard format (conversion only, nothing recomputed)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(data.table))

std_dir <- "results/standard"
dir.create(std_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

to_long <- function(path, value_name) {
  m <- as.matrix(read.csv(path, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
  idx <- which(m > 0, arr.ind = TRUE)
  out <- data.table(cell_type = rownames(m)[idx[, "row"]], x = colnames(m)[idx[, "col"]])
  setnames(out, "x", value_name)
  setorderv(out, c("cell_type", value_name))
  list(table = out, celltypes = rownames(m))
}

lig <- to_long("results/racing_input/Lmatrix_Gide.csv", "ligand")
rec <- to_long("results/racing_input/Rmatrix_Gide.csv", "receptor")
stopifnot(setequal(lig$celltypes, rec$celltypes))
fwrite(lig$table, file.path(std_dir, "ligands.csv"))
fwrite(rec$table, file.path(std_dir, "receptors.csv"))

# Undirected raw kernel features, as returned by compute_racing_kernel(remove_direction = TRUE)
und <- read.csv("results/kernel/direct_communication_undirected_raw.csv",
                row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
celltypes <- lig$celltypes
stopifnot(!any(grepl("_", celltypes)))  # so "Dir_A_B" splits unambiguously
parts <- strsplit(sub("^Dir_", "", colnames(und)), "_", fixed = TRUE)
stopifnot(all(lengths(parts) == 2), all(unlist(parts) %in% celltypes))
new_names <- vapply(parts, function(p) paste(p[1], "-", p[2]), character(1))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(new_names))

# read-only consistency check against the directed raw features (A-B = A->B + B->A, A-A = 2 * A->A)
